# Grammarly vs LanguageTool: Is it really worth paying €12/month?

Are you hesitating between Grammarly Premium (€12/month) and LanguageTool Premium (€5/month)? Or are you wondering if the free version is enough? This guide gives you the exact calculation to know which spell checker to choose as a freelancer.

**Spoiler**: 80% of freelancers pay for a spell checker but only use 30% of its features. Here's how to avoid this trap.

---

## TL;DR: Which checker to choose?

**Stay free** (Grammarly or LanguageTool) if:
- You write less than 10,000 words/month
- You write mainly in French (the free versions are very good)
- You don't need advanced style suggestions

**Pay for LanguageTool Premium (€5/month)** if:
- You write regularly in French AND English
- You want rephrasing suggestions
- You need to detect false friends and Anglicisms

**Pay for Grammarly Premium (€12/month)** if:
- You write mainly in English (> 20,000 words/month)
- You need plagiarism detection
- You want an integrated AI writing assistant

**Cancel everything** if:
- You write less than 5,000 words/month
- Integrated checkers (Word, Google Docs) are sufficient for you
- You already have [ChatGPT Plus](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile) (which can correct your texts)

---

## The real differences between Grammarly and LanguageTool

### Full comparative table

| Feature | Grammarly Free | Grammarly Premium | LanguageTool Free | LanguageTool Premium |
|-----------------|-------------------|-------------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| **Price** | Free | €12/month | Free | €5/month |
| **Spell check** | ✅ Excellent | ✅ Excellent | ✅ Excellent | ✅ Excellent |
| **Grammar check** | ✅ Good | ✅ Excellent | ✅ Good | ✅ Excellent |
| **Style suggestions** | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ❌ Limited | ✅ Yes |
| **Plagiarism detection** | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **AI Rephrasing** | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| **Languages supported** | English only | English only | 30+ languages | 30+ languages |
| **Character limit** | Unlimited | Unlimited | 10,000 characters | 60,000 characters |
| **Browser integration** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Word integration** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |

### What no one tells you

**Grammarly** is better for:
- English (it's its core business)
- Plagiarism detection (essential for students/researchers)
- Integration with Gmail, LinkedIn, Google Docs

**LanguageTool** is better for:
- French (and 30+ other languages)
- Detecting Anglicisms and false friends
- Value for money (€5/month vs €12/month)

---

## The real ROI calculation

### Scenario 1: Freelance writer (French)

**Profile:**
- You write 30,000 words/month in French
- You write blog posts, newsletters, web pages
- You charge €0.10/word on average

**Verdict: LanguageTool Premium (€5/month)**

**Why?** LanguageTool is much better than Grammarly for French. It detects Anglicisms, false friends, and specific French style errors.

**ROI:** If LanguageTool saves you 1 hour/month (by avoiding back-and-forth with your clients), you earn €10 (1 hour at €10/hour). The cost is €5/month. **ROI: 100%**.

**Savings vs Grammarly: €84/year** (€12 - €5 = €7/month × 12 months)

---

### Scenario 2: Freelance copywriter (English)

**Profile:**
- You write 50,000 words/month in English
- You write landing pages, marketing emails, video scripts
- You charge €0.15/word on average

**Verdict: Grammarly Premium (€12/month)**

**Why?** Grammarly is the best English checker on the market. Its style and tone suggestions are unbeatable for copywriting.

**ROI:** If Grammarly saves you 30 minutes/month (by improving the quality of your texts), you earn €7.50 (0.5 hours at €15/hour). The cost is €12/month. **ROI: -37%** (but you gain in quality).

**Alternative:** If you already have [ChatGPT Plus](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile) (€20/month), use it to correct your texts. You save €12/month.

---

### Scenario 3: Freelance consultant (emails + reports)

**Profile:**
- You write 5,000 words/month (emails, reports, presentations)
- You write in French and English
- You charge €100/hour on average

**Verdict: STAY FREE**

**Why?** You write too little to justify a subscription. Integrated checkers (Word, Google Docs) + free LanguageTool are sufficient.

**Savings: €144/year** (€12/month × 12 months)

**Alternative:** If you already have [ChatGPT Plus](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile), ask it to correct your emails and reports. It's free (included in the subscription).

---

## The 3 mistakes that lead to unnecessarily paying for a checker

### Mistake 1: Paying for features you never use

**The trap:** You pay for Grammarly Premium for plagiarism detection, but you never use it.

**The solution:** Switch to LanguageTool Premium (€5/month) or stay free. Plagiarism detection is only useful for students, researchers, or journalists.

**Savings: €84/year**

---

### Mistake 2: Paying for Grammarly to write in French

**The trap:** You pay for Grammarly Premium (€12/month) even though you write primarily in French.

**The solution:** Switch to LanguageTool Premium (€5/month). It is much better for French and costs half as much.

**Savings: €84/year**

---

### Mistake 3: Paying for a checker when you already have ChatGPT Plus

**The trap:** You pay for Grammarly Premium (€12/month) + [ChatGPT Plus](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile) (€20/month) = €32/month.

**The solution:** Use ChatGPT to correct your texts. Copy-paste your text and ask: "Correct spelling and grammar mistakes, and improve the style."

**Savings: €144/year** (€12/month × 12 months)

---

## Free alternatives

Before paying for a checker, test these free alternatives:

### 1. Integrated checkers (Word, Google Docs)

**For whom?** Freelancers who write less than 5,000 words/month.

**Advantages:**
- Free and already installed
- Detects 80% of spelling and grammar mistakes
- Works offline

**Disadvantage:** No advanced style suggestions.

---

### 2. [ChatGPT](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile) (free or €20/month)

**For whom?** Freelancers who already have ChatGPT Plus for other uses.

**Advantages:**
- Corrects spelling, grammar, AND improves style
- Can completely rephrase your texts
- Free if you already have the subscription

**Disadvantage:** No browser integration (you have to copy-paste).

---

### 3. Antidote (€115 one-time purchase)

**For whom?** Professional writers who write in French.

**Advantages:**
- One-time purchase (no subscription)
- The best French checker on the market
- Integrated dictionaries and linguistic guides

**Disadvantage:** Expensive to buy (€115), but profitable in the long run (vs €60/year for LanguageTool).

---

## The killer use case for freelancers

There is ONE case where a paid checker becomes indispensable: **writing in English for international clients**.

If you are a consultant, copywriter, or freelance writer and you write in English for American or British clients, Grammarly Premium is a worthwhile investment.

**Why?** Because your English-speaking clients immediately detect grammar and style errors. A single mistake can make you lose a client worth €10,000/year.

**ROI:** If Grammarly prevents you from losing 1 client/year, you earn €10,000 - €144 (Grammarly cost) = **€9,856**.

---

## Grammarly vs LanguageTool: The detailed match

### Spell check

**Winner: Tie**

Both tools detect 99% of spelling mistakes. No noticeable difference.

---

### Grammar check

**Winner: Grammarly (for English), LanguageTool (for French)**

Grammarly is better at detecting complex grammatical errors in English (tense agreement, passive voice, etc.).

LanguageTool is better for French (agreements, conjugations, false friends).

---

### Style suggestions

**Winner: Grammarly**

Grammarly Premium offers advanced style suggestions (tone, clarity, conciseness, engagement). LanguageTool Premium is less sophisticated on this point.

---

### AI Rephrasing

**Winner: Grammarly**

Grammarly Premium integrates an AI assistant that can completely rephrase your sentences. LanguageTool Premium offers rephrasing, but it's less sophisticated.

**Alternative:** Use [ChatGPT](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile) to rephrase your texts. It's free (or €20/month if you already have the subscription).

---

### Plagiarism detection

**Winner: Grammarly**

Grammarly Premium includes a plagiarism detector. LanguageTool does not offer this feature.

**For whom?** Students, researchers, journalists. Useless for 90% of freelancers.

---

### Languages supported

**Winner: LanguageTool**

LanguageTool supports 30+ languages (French, English, Spanish, German, Italian, etc.). Grammarly only supports English.

---

### Price

**Winner: LanguageTool**

LanguageTool Premium costs €5/month. Grammarly Premium costs €12/month. **Savings: €84/year**.

---

## Checklist: Which checker to choose?

Use this checklist to decide in 2 minutes:

**Stay free if:**
- [ ] You write less than 10,000 words/month
- [ ] You write mainly in French
- [ ] Integrated checkers (Word, Google Docs) are sufficient for you
- [ ] You already have [ChatGPT Plus](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile) to correct your texts

**Pay for LanguageTool Premium (€5/month) if:**
- [ ] You write regularly in French AND English
- [ ] You want rephrasing suggestions
- [ ] You need to detect false friends and Anglicisms
- [ ] You want the best value for money

**Pay for Grammarly Premium (€12/month) if:**
- [ ] You write mainly in English (> 20,000 words/month)
- [ ] You need plagiarism detection
- [ ] You want an integrated AI writing assistant
- [ ] You write for demanding English-speaking clients

**Buy Antidote (€115 one-time purchase) if:**
- [ ] You are a professional French writer
- [ ] You want a tool without a subscription
- [ ] You need dictionaries and linguistic guides

---

## Conclusion: The 10,000 words/month rule

Here's the simple rule: **Only pay for a checker if you write more than 10,000 words/month.**

How to calculate?
- If you write 10,000 words/month at €0.10/word = €1,000/month revenue
- If a checker saves you 1 hour/month (by avoiding back-and-forth with your clients) = €10-€20 gain
- Cost: €5-€12/month
- **ROI: 50-150%**

Otherwise, stay free or use [ChatGPT](/article/chatgpt-plus-utile-ou-inutile) to correct your texts.

# Toggl Track: Free or Paid? The Complete Guide for Freelancers

**Toggl Track is the most popular time tracking tool among freelancers.** But is it really worth paying €9/month for the Pro version? Is the free version sufficient? And when exactly does upgrading to paid become profitable?

This guide gives you the exact calculation to decide whether Toggl Track free or paid fits your freelance situation.

## TL;DR: Free or Paid in 3 Questions

**1. Do you need detailed reports by project/client?**
- **No** → Free is sufficient
- **Yes** → Paid recommended (unlimited reports)

**2. Are you managing multiple clients simultaneously?**
- **1-2 clients** → Free is sufficient
- **3+ clients** → Paid (better organization)

**3. Do you charge hourly or fixed price?**
- **Fixed price** → Free is sufficient (personal tracking)
- **Hourly** → Paid (client reports, precision)

## Toggl Track Free vs Paid Comparison Table

| Feature | Free | Pro (€9/month) | Team (€20/month) |
|---------|------|----------------|------------------|
| **Number of projects** | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Number of clients** | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Reports** | Basic (1 only) | Detailed (unlimited) | Detailed + team management |
| **Tags** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Integrations** | 50+ | 50+ | 50+ |
| **Data export** | CSV/PDF | CSV/PDF/JSON | CSV/PDF/JSON |
| **History** | 90 days | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Team** | No | No | Yes (up to 5) |
| **Support** | Email | Priority email | Priority email |
| **Monthly cost** | €0 | €9 | €20 |

## Toggl Track Free: Sufficient for 80% of Freelancers

The free version of Toggl Track is **surprisingly complete**. Here's what you can do:

### Included Features (Free)

**Real-time time tracking**: Click "Start", work, click "Stop". Toggl automatically records the duration. You can also manually add time (useful for forgotten tasks).

**Organization by projects and clients**: Create as many projects as you want (ChatGPT, Notion, Webflow, etc.). Each project can be linked to a client. Toggl free handles this perfectly.

**Tags and categories**: Tag each session (e.g., "Development", "Meeting", "Support"). Useful for analyzing where your time really goes.

**Basic reports**: One report available (weekly/monthly view of time by project). Sufficient to see where you spent your time.

**Integrations**: Toggl integrates with 50+ tools (Slack, Notion, Asana, Jira, Zapier, etc.). The free version has access to all integrations.

**90-day history**: You can view and edit entries from the last 90 days. Beyond that, data is archived (but not deleted).

### Use Cases: When Free is Sufficient

**Profile 1: Solo freelancer with 1-2 clients**

You work for 2-3 regular clients and simply want to track your time for your own productivity. The free version is **perfect**. A single report is enough to see your time by project.

**Example**: You work 20h/week for Client A and 15h/week for Client B. Toggl free shows you exactly this breakdown. Cost: €0/month.

**Profile 2: Freelancer who charges fixed price**

You charge per project (e.g., "Build a website: €2000"), not hourly. You use Toggl to understand your personal productivity, not to bill. Free is sufficient.

**Example**: You build a website in 40 hours. Toggl free shows you spent 40 hours on this project. You know you charged €2000 for 40 hours = €50/hour. Cost: €0/month.

**Profile 3: Freelancer testing the tool**

You're not sure if time tracking will be useful. Start free for 1 month. If you use it daily, upgrade to paid. Otherwise, stay free.

**Example**: You start tracking your time. After 1 month, you realize you never check the reports. Stay free. Cost: €0/month.

## Toggl Track Paid (€9/month): When It's Profitable

The Pro version costs **€9/month** (or €90/year if you pay annually = €7.50/month). Here's what you gain:

### Additional Features (Pro)

**Unlimited reports**: Instead of one basic report, you can create as many reports as you want. Example: one report per client, one per task type, one per week, etc.

**Detailed reports**: Pro reports include charts, trends, and analysis. You can see exactly where your time goes (by day, week, month).

**Advanced export**: Export your data as JSON (useful for custom integrations), not just CSV/PDF.

**Unlimited history**: Access all your data since the day you created your account (not limited to 90 days).

**Priority support**: Access to priority email support (24-hour response instead of 48 hours).

### Use Cases: When Paid is Profitable

**Profile 1: Freelancer who charges hourly**

You charge clients hourly (e.g., €50/hour). You need detailed reports to bill precisely and show clients where you spent your time. The Pro version is **essential**.

**ROI calculation**: If you charge €50/hour and Toggl Pro saves you 1 hour/month in accurate billing (avoiding oversights, approximations), you gain €50. Toggl Pro costs €9/month. ROI = €50 - €9 = €41/month net benefit.

**Verdict**: Paid = profitable.

**Profile 2: Freelancer with 5+ simultaneous clients**

You manage 5-10 clients at the same time. You need detailed reports for each client to analyze your productivity per client and bill precisely. The Pro version is **very useful**.

**Example**: Client A (20h/month), Client B (15h/month), Client C (10h/month), Client D (8h/month), Client E (7h/month). With Toggl Pro, you create one report per client and see exactly your time for each.

**Verdict**: Paid = very useful.

**Profile 3: Freelancer who wants to analyze productivity**

You want to understand your work patterns: when are you most productive? Which projects take the most time? Toggl Pro offers charts and analysis to help you optimize.

**Example**: You discover that client meetings take 8h/week (20% of your time). You decide to group them into 2 sessions/week instead of 4. You gain 4h/week = €200/month (at €50/hour).

**Verdict**: Paid = very profitable if you act on the insights.

## Alternatives to Toggl Track

If you're looking for other time tracking tools, here are the best alternatives:

### Clockify (Free or €9/month)

**Advantages**: Unlimited free (no project/report limits like Toggl). Interface similar to Toggl. Many integrations.

**Disadvantages**: Less popular than Toggl. Fewer report templates.

**Verdict**: Clockify free = better than Toggl free if you need unlimited reports. Cost: €0/month.

### Harvest (€12/month)

**Advantages**: Time tracking + integrated invoicing. Very professional. Detailed reports.

**Disadvantages**: More expensive than Toggl. Overkill for simple freelancers.

**Verdict**: Harvest = best if you want time tracking + invoicing in one tool. Cost: €12/month.

### Everhour (€5/month)

**Advantages**: Cheaper than Toggl. Excellent Asana/Jira/Trello integrations. Detailed reports.

**Disadvantages**: Less known than Toggl. Fewer templates.

**Verdict**: Everhour = best for freelancers using Asana/Jira. Cost: €5/month.

### Google Sheets + manual formulas (Free)

**Advantages**: Free. Completely customizable.

**Disadvantages**: No real-time tracking. Tedious to maintain. No integrations.

**Verdict**: Google Sheets = for purists who dislike SaaS tools. Cost: €0/month.

## The Verdict: Toggl Track Free or Paid?

### Stay free if:

- You have **1-3 clients** maximum
- You charge **fixed price**, not hourly
- You don't need **detailed reports** for your clients
- You use Toggl mainly for **your personal productivity**
- You have a **very tight budget** (beginner freelancer)

**Cost**: €0/month. **Benefit**: Time tracking, organization by projects, integrations.

### Upgrade to paid if:

- You have **5+ simultaneous clients**
- You charge **hourly** and need precise reports
- You want to **analyze your productivity** with charts and trends
- You need to **bill your clients** with detailed reports
- You have a **€9/month budget** (less than 1 hour of work/month)

**Cost**: €9/month. **Benefit**: Unlimited reports, unlimited history, detailed analysis, priority support.

## 3 Mistakes to Avoid with Toggl Track

### Mistake 1: Tracking "everything" without discipline

**The trap**: You track every minute (meetings, coffee, breaks), creating noise. After 1 month, you have 200 entries and don't know what to do with them.

**The solution**: Track only **billable work or important projects**. Ignore breaks, personal emails, minor admin tasks.

**Example**: Track "Website Development" (billable), not "Read emails" (non-billable).

### Mistake 2: Creating too many projects/tags

**The trap**: You create 50 projects and 100 tags. After 1 month, you don't know where to categorize your time.

**The solution**: Keep **maximum 10 projects** and **maximum 20 tags**. Group small projects together.

**Example**: Instead of "Project A", "Project B", "Project C", create "Client A" and tag by work type (Development, Design, Support).

### Mistake 3: Paying for Toggl Pro without using it

**The trap**: You pay €9/month but never check Pro reports. That's wasted money.

**The solution**: Start free. After 1 month, if you regularly check reports and need more detail, upgrade to paid.

**Savings**: €9/month = €108/year.

## Conclusion: Toggl Track Free is Sufficient for 80% of Freelancers

**Toggl Track free** is an excellent tool for freelancers who want to track their time without paying. It offers all essential features: real-time tracking, organization by projects, tags, integrations, and a basic report.

**Toggl Track paid** (€9/month) becomes profitable if you charge hourly, have 5+ clients, or want to analyze your productivity in detail.

**Our recommendation**: Start free. After 1 month, evaluate if you need detailed reports. If yes, upgrade to paid. If no, stay free.

**Total cost for 1 year**: €0 (free) or €108 (paid) = less than 1 hour of work/month.

# You manage 3 clients simultaneously: Is free Notion really enough for you?

## The scene

It's 2 PM. You have 3 active clients right now. Your phone is blowing up with Slack messages. In your head, it's chaos: where's client A's brief? What was client B's deadline? You forgot to invoice client C last week.

You open Notion. Once again, you ask yourself: "Do I really need to pay $10/month for the Pro version? Isn't the free one enough for me?"

That's exactly the question you need to ask yourself. And contrary to what you might think, the answer isn't "it depends."

---

## The real problem: you confuse "having a tool" with "having real organization"

Most freelancers think Notion Pro will save them. That with advanced templates and team permissions, everything will magically organize itself.

False.

The problem isn't Notion. The problem is that you don't have a system. You haphazardly add briefs, you create databases without structure, and you end up with 47 different pages where you can't find anything anymore.

Free Notion can handle 3 clients. Notion Pro can too. The difference? Notion Pro allows you to do things you probably don't need to do.

---

## What free Notion does really well (and what it doesn't)

### ✅ What free Notion allows you to do

- **Create unlimited databases**: You can have one database per client, one for tasks, one for invoices. No limit.
- **Use templates**: Notion offers hundreds of them. Free. They're good.
- **Collaborate with guests**: You can invite your clients or subcontractors. Free. Up to 5 guests per page.
- **Create formulas and relations**: Yes, even in the free version. You can link your tasks to your projects, calculate dates, anything you want.
- **Export to PDF**: Useful for sending client reports.

### ❌ What free Notion does not allow you to do

- **Advanced permissions**: In the free version, either someone has access to everything, or they have access to nothing. No "read-only" for a specific client.
- **API**: If you want to connect Notion to other tools (Zapier, Make, etc.), Pro is the minimum.
- **Advanced synced blocks**: Synced blocks exist in the free version, but they are limited.
- **Unlimited guests**: You are limited to 5 guests per page. If you have 10 clients, that's a problem.

**The truth?** For 3 clients, you don't need any of these Pro features.

---

## The ROI calculation: when does Notion Pro pay for itself?

Let's look at the numbers.

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Notion Pro | $10/month = €120/year |
| Free Notion | €0 |
| **Difference** | **€120/year** |

Now, the real question: **How much time does Notion Pro save you per month?**

Honestly? For 3 clients, probably 0 hours. Advanced permissions only save you time if you have a real team. The API only saves you time if you truly automate your workflows.

But wait. Maybe you have a specific case.

### Case 1: You have 5+ clients and you need to invite them all to Notion

**Cost of the problem:** You are limited to 5 guests per page. If you have 6 clients, you can't invite them all.

**Free solution:** Create a public page per client. Not sexy, but it works.

**Pro solution:** Advanced permissions. Each client only sees their own folder.

**Time saved:** 30 minutes per month (no manual access management).

**ROI:** €120/year for 6h/year = €20/hour saved. This is profitable if you charge >€20/h.

### Case 2: You want to automate your workflows with Zapier or Make

**Cost of the problem:** Without an API (free), you cannot connect Notion to your other tools.

**Free solution:** Do things manually. Copy-paste. Annoying.

**Pro solution:** API. Connect Notion to Zapier. Automate task addition, invoice creation, etc.

**Time saved:** 2-3 hours per month (depending on your level of automation).

**ROI:** €120/year for 24-36h/year = €3.5-5/hour saved. This is profitable if you charge >€5/h. (Spoiler: you charge more.)

---

## ToolTrim's recommendation

**No. You don't need Notion Pro if you manage fewer than 5 active projects.**

Here's why:

1.  **Free Notion does 95% of the work.** The remaining 5% (advanced permissions, API) only concern you if you have a real team or if you are a power user.

2.  **The time saved is minimal.** Even with Pro, you don't gain 2h/month. That's honest.

3.  **There are better alternatives for specific cases.** If you need advanced permissions, check out Airtable (free with permissions). If you need an API, check out Coda (free with API).

**When you should upgrade to Pro:**

-   You have 6+ clients and you invite them all to Notion
-   You truly automate your workflows (Zapier, Make, etc.)
-   You charge >€50/h and you want to save 2h/month

**Until then, stay free. Seriously.**

---

## What we would do in your place

If you manage 3 clients with free Notion:

1.  **Create a database per client.** Not a page per client. A database. With a relation to a "Projects" database.

2.  **Use Notion templates.** There's a good one for "Client Management." Start there.

3.  **Add an "Invoices" database.** Link it to your clients. Add a formula to calculate amounts.

4.  **Export a PDF report every month.** Send it to your clients. It looks professional.

5.  **Revisit the question in 6 months.** If you have 6+ clients, we'll talk again.

---

## Conclusion

Notion Pro costs €120/year. For 3 clients, you won't gain €120 in productivity. The free version is enough for you. Use that money for something else. Seriously.

# You just signed your 2nd client: do you need Calendly Pro?

## The scene

It's Tuesday morning. You've just signed your 2nd client. Congratulations. But now, you need to manage appointments with two different people. One prefers morning calls. The other, afternoon. One is in a different time zone. The other wants 30-min calls, not 1h.

You think: "Maybe Calendly Pro would help me manage all this?"

Spoiler: no. Not yet.

---

## The real problem: you're confusing "managing appointments" with "having a professional calendar system"

Most freelancers think Calendly Pro will save them. That with unlimited event types and custom reminders, everything will organize itself.

False.

The problem isn't Calendly. The problem is that you don't have a routine for calls. You accept anytime. You forget to confirm appointments. You arrive late.

Free Calendly can handle 2 clients. Calendly Pro can too. The difference? Calendly Pro allows you to do things you probably don't need to do.

---

## What free Calendly does really well (and what it doesn't)

### ✅ What free Calendly allows you to do

- **Create 1 event type**: You can create a "30 min call" or "1h call" link. Just one. That's enough for 2 clients.
- **Sync with Google Calendar or Outlook**: Your Calendly appointments appear in your calendar. Free.
- **Send reminders**: Calendly automatically sends a reminder 24 hours before. Free.
- **Display your availability**: You can say "I'm available Monday and Wednesday, 10 am-12 pm". Free.
- **Embed the link everywhere**: On your website, in your email signature, on LinkedIn. Free.

### ❌ What free Calendly doesn't allow you to do

- **Create multiple event types**: Need a "30 min call" AND a "1h call"? That's Pro.
- **Set prices**: If you want to sell slots (e.g., €50 consultation), that's Pro.
- **Custom reminders**: You can send a reminder 24 hours before. But not "SMS 1h before + email 24h before". That's Pro.
- **Group appointments**: If you want to prevent 2 clients from booking at the same time, that's Pro.
- **Advanced branding**: You can add your logo. But not customize colors. That's Pro.

**The truth?** For 2 clients, you don't need any of these Pro features.

---

## The ROI calculation: when does Calendly Pro pay for itself?

Let's look at the numbers.

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Calendly Pro | $10/month = €120/year |
| Free Calendly | €0 |
| **Difference** | **€120/year** |

Now, the real question: **How much time does Calendly Pro save you per month?**

Honestly? For 2 clients, probably 0 hours. Unlimited event types only save you time if you have 5+ different services. Custom reminders only save you time if you truly forget your appointments.

But wait. Maybe you have a specific case.

### Case 1: You have 3+ different event types

**Cost of the problem:** You are limited to 1 type for free. If you want "30 min call", "1h call" AND "Paid consultation", you can't.

**Free solution:** Create 3 different Calendly links. Share the correct link with each client. Not sexy, but it works.

**Pro solution:** All types on a single link. The client chooses.

**Time saved:** 15 minutes per month (no manual link management).

**ROI:** €120/year for 3h/year = €40/hour saved. This is profitable if you charge >€40/h.

### Case 2: You want to sell slots (paid consultation)

**Cost of the problem:** Free Calendly doesn't allow you to sell slots. You have to use another tool (Stripe, Gumroad, etc.).

**Free solution:** Use Stripe + Calendly. Two tools. More complicated.

**Pro solution:** Calendly Pro + Stripe. Native integration. One tool.

**Time saved:** 30 minutes per month (no manual synchronization).

**ROI:** €120/year for 6h/year = €20/hour saved. This is profitable if you charge >€20/h.

---

## The ToolTrim recommendation

**No. You don't need Calendly Pro if you have fewer than 3 different event types.**

Here's why:

1.  **Free Calendly does 95% of the work.** The remaining 5% (unlimited types, selling slots) only concerns you if you have a truly diversified offering.

2.  **The time saved is minimal.** Even with Pro, you won't save 30 min/month. That's being honest.

3.  **There are better alternatives for specific cases.** If you want to sell slots, look at Acuity Scheduling (free with integrated selling). If you want multiple types, look at Cal.com (free and open source).

**When you should upgrade to Pro:**

-   You have 3+ different event types
-   You want to sell slots directly within Calendly
-   You charge >€40/h and want to save 15 min/month

**Until then, stay free. Seriously.**

---

## What we would do in your place

If you're managing 2 clients with free Calendly:

1.  **Create a single event type.** "30 min call" or "1h call". Choose one. Just one.

2.  **Sync with Google Calendar.** Free Calendly does this automatically. Your appointments appear in your calendar.

3.  **Add a 15 min buffer after each call.** Calendly allows you to say "after each appointment, block 15 min". Use that.

4.  **Share the link everywhere.** On your website, in your email signature, on LinkedIn. A single link.

5.  **Revisit the question in 6 months.** If you have 3+ event types, we'll talk again.

---

Calendly Pro costs €120/year. For 2 clients, you won't gain €120 in productivity. The free version is enough for you. Use that money for something else. Really.

# You spend 2 hours/day on repetitive tasks: Does ChatGPT Plus really make a difference?

## The scene

It's 9 AM. You open your computer. You have 15 emails to deal with. 3 client briefs to review. 2 commercial proposals to draft. A presentation to prepare.

You think: "If I used ChatGPT Plus, I'd have more features. Could I do all this faster?"

Maybe. But honestly? Probably not.

---

## The real problem: you're confusing "having better AI" with "having a better work system"

Most freelancers think ChatGPT Plus will save them. That with GPT-4 and plugins, everything will speed up.

False.

The problem isn't ChatGPT. The problem is that you don't have templates. You don't have reusable prompts. You write every email as if it were the first time.

Free ChatGPT can do 95% of the work. ChatGPT Plus can too. The difference? ChatGPT Plus is faster and smarter. But for a solo freelancer, it's often a luxury.

---

## What free ChatGPT does really well (and what it doesn't)

### ✅ What free ChatGPT allows you to do

- **Draft emails**: Free ChatGPT can draft a professional email in 10 seconds. It works.
- **Proofread texts**: You can copy-paste a text and ask ChatGPT to correct it. Free.
- **Generate ideas**: You can ask for 10 content ideas for LinkedIn. Free.
- **Explain concepts**: Don't understand a technical concept? Free ChatGPT can explain it.
- **Translate**: Free ChatGPT translates very well. Better than Google Translate.

### ❌ What free ChatGPT doesn't allow you to do

- **Use GPT-4**: Free ChatGPT uses GPT-3.5. It's slower and less intelligent.
- **Create images**: Free ChatGPT cannot create images. No more need for Midjourney for a simple image.
- **Use plugins**: Want to connect ChatGPT to Google Sheets or Zapier? That's Plus.
- **Priority access**: When ChatGPT is overloaded, Plus users get priority.
- **Use "Code Interpreter" mode**: Want ChatGPT to write and execute code? That's Plus.

**The truth?** For a solo freelancer, you don't need any of these Plus features.

---

## The ROI calculation: When does ChatGPT Plus pay for itself?

Let's look at the numbers.

| Element | Cost |
|---|---|
| ChatGPT Plus | $20/month = €240/year |
| Free ChatGPT | €0 |
| **Difference** | **€240/year** |

Now, the real question: **How much time does ChatGPT Plus save you per month?**

That's the key question. Because ChatGPT Plus isn't 2x faster than the free version. It might be 20-30% faster.

### Case 1: You use ChatGPT 2h/day to draft and proofread

**Current time:** 2h/day = 40h/month

**With free ChatGPT:** You save 1h/day (instead of 2h). So 1h/day = 20h/month.

**With ChatGPT Plus:** You save 1h15 min/day (GPT-4 is 20% faster). So 1h15/day = 25h/month.

**Difference:** 25h - 20h = 5h/month

**ROI:** €240/year for 60h/year = €4/hour saved. It's profitable if you charge >€4/h. (Spoiler: you charge more.)

**Verdict:** Yes, it's profitable. But just barely.

### Case 2: You use ChatGPT 30 min/day

**Current time:** 30 min/day = 10h/month

**With free ChatGPT:** You save 15 min/day. So 15 min/day = 5h/month.

**With ChatGPT Plus:** You save 18 min/day (20% faster). So 18 min/day = 6h/month.

**Difference:** 6h - 5h = 1h/month

**ROI:** €240/year for 12h/year = €20/hour saved. It's profitable if you charge >€20/h.

**Verdict:** It's profitable. But very barely.

### Case 3: You want to create images with ChatGPT Plus

**Cost of the problem:** Free ChatGPT cannot create images. You have to use Midjourney ($15/month) or DALL-E ($0.02 per image).

**Free solution:** Use Midjourney. $15/month.

**Plus solution:** ChatGPT Plus + integrated DALL-E. $20/month.

**Time saved:** 30 min/month (no tool switching).

**ROI:** €20/year for 6h/year = €3.33/hour saved. It's profitable if you charge >€3.33/h.

**Verdict:** Yes, it's profitable. But you're mostly saving friction, not time.

---

## ToolTrim's recommendation

**Yes, ChatGPT Plus pays for itself. But only if you use ChatGPT 2h+/day.**

Here's why:

1. **ChatGPT Plus is 20-30% faster.** That's true. But it's not 2x faster.

2. **The time saved depends on your usage.** If you use ChatGPT 30 min/day, you save 1h/month. If you use it 2h/day, you save 5h/month.

3. **You need to charge >€20/h for it to be truly profitable.** If you charge €50/h, yes, it's a no-brainer. If you charge €15/h, it's just barely.

**When you should upgrade to Plus:**

- You use ChatGPT 2h+/day
- You charge >€30/h
- You want to create images directly in ChatGPT

**Until then, stay free. Seriously.**

---

## What we would do in your place

If you use free ChatGPT:

1. **Create prompt templates.** Save your best prompts in a document. Reuse them.

2. **Use ChatGPT for repetitive tasks.** Emails, corrections, translations. Not for original creation.

3. **Combine free ChatGPT with other tools.** ChatGPT for writing + Grammarly for proofreading + Canva for images.

4. **Measure your time saved.** For 1 week, note how much time you gain with ChatGPT. Then decide if Plus is worth it.

5. **Revisit the question in 3 months.** If you use ChatGPT 2h+/day, upgrade to Plus.

---

## Conclusion

ChatGPT Plus costs €240/year. If you use ChatGPT 30 min/day, you won't gain €240 in productivity. The free version is enough for you. Use that money for something else. Seriously.

But if you use ChatGPT 2h+/day? Then Plus pays for itself. That's fair.

# You received client feedback about a mistake: Is Grammarly Premium worth it?

## The Scene

It's Thursday morning. You receive an email from your client. "By the way, I noticed a small mistake in the document you sent me. Nothing serious, but I thought you'd want to know."

Your heart stops. A mistake. You, a professional freelancer, sent a document with a mistake.

You think: "Maybe Grammarly Premium would have caught that mistake?"

Spoiler: yes, probably. But is it worth the cost?

---

Wrong.

The problem isn't Grammarly. The problem is that you don't have a proofreading process. You send your documents without reviewing them. You trust free Grammarly. And sometimes, you make mistakes.

- **Work everywhere**: Gmail, Google Docs, LinkedIn, Twitter, etc. Free.

### ❌ What free Grammarly does not allow you to do

- **Tone suggestions**: Do you want your text to be more "professional" or more "friendly"? That's Premium.
- **Plagiarism detection**: Do you want to check if your text is copied? That's Premium.
- **Advanced suggestions**: "This paragraph is too long. Split it in two." That's Premium.
- **Style checks**: "You use too much passive voice. Switch to active voice." That's Premium.
- **Detailed reports**: Grammarly Premium gives you a report on your most frequent errors.

**The truth?** For a solo freelancer, you don't need any of these Premium features.

Let's look at the numbers.

|---|---|
| Grammarly Premium | €12/month = €144/year |
| Free Grammarly | €0 |
| **Difference** | **€144/year** |

Now, the real question: **How much time does Grammarly Premium save you per month?**

Honestly? Probably 0 hours. Tone suggestions don't save you time. They just make you write "better" according to Grammarly.

But wait. Maybe you have a specific case.

### Case 1: You write a lot (2000+ words/day) and need to check the tone

**Cost of the problem:** You send texts with an inconsistent tone. Sometimes too formal, sometimes too casual.

**Free solution:** Manual proofreading. Take 30 min per document.

**Premium solution:** Grammarly Premium suggests adjusting the tone. You save 15 min per document.

**Time saved:** If you write 5 documents/month, you save 1h15 min/month.

**ROI:** €144/year for 15h/year = €9.6/hour saved. This is profitable if you charge >€10/h.

**Verdict:** Yes, it's profitable. But just barely.

### Case 2: You want to check that you haven't copied other texts

**Cost of the problem:** You have to manually check that your text isn't plagiarized. Or use Copyscape (free but basic).

**Free solution:** Use Copyscape. Free. But basic.

**Premium solution:** Grammarly Premium includes plagiarism checking. More advanced.

**Time saved:** 10 min per document. If you write 5 documents/month, you save 50 min/month.

**ROI:** €144/year for 10h/year = €14.4/hour saved. This is profitable if you charge >€15/h.

**Verdict:** Yes, it's profitable. But just barely.

### Case 3: You receive client feedback on the tone of your texts

**Free solution:** Manual proofreading and adjusting the tone. 30 min per document.

**Premium solution:** Grammarly Premium suggests adjusting the tone. You save 15 min per document.

**Time saved:** If you write 5 documents/month, you save 1h15 min/month.

**Verdict:** Yes, it's profitable. But just barely.

## The ToolTrim Recommendation

Here's why:

1. **Free Grammarly detects 90% of errors.** The remaining 10% are rare and often contextual.

2. **Time saved depends on your usage.** If you write 500 words/day, you save nothing. If you write 2000+ words/day, you save 1-2h/month.

4. **Create a proofreading checklist.** Before sending a document, check: spelling, grammar, punctuation, tone, length. Free.

# You've just signed your first client: how should you get paid?

## The scene

It's Monday morning. You've just signed your first client. Congratulations. But now, you need to get paid. Your client asks: "How do you want me to pay you?"

You think: "Bank transfer? Stripe? PayPal? What's best?"

That's a good question. And the answer isn't "it depends."

---

## The real problem: you're confusing "receiving money" with "receiving money professionally"

Most freelancers think Stripe will save them. That with card payments and automatic invoices, everything will sort itself out.

Wrong.

The problem isn't Stripe. The problem is that you don't have a invoicing process. You send an invoice randomly. You wait for the client to pay you. You forget to follow up.

Bank transfer can work. Stripe too. The difference? Stripe forces you to be professional.

---

## What bank transfer does really well (and what it doesn't)

### ✅ What bank transfer allows you to do

- **Receive money for free**: No fees. The money arrives directly in your account.
- **No third party**: It's between you and your client. No intermediary.
- **Easy to set up**: You give your IBAN. That's it.
- **No limit**: You can receive €10 or €100,000. No limit.

### ❌ What bank transfer doesn't allow you to do

- **Card payments**: Your client must have a bank account and know how to make a transfer. Not all clients do.
- **Easy international payments**: If your client is abroad, transfer fees can be high.
- **Automation**: You have to manually follow up if the client forgets to pay.
- **Automatic invoices**: You have to send invoices manually.
- **Reports**: You have to manage your payments manually in a spreadsheet.

**The truth?** For 1 client, bank transfer is enough.

---

## What Stripe does really well (and what it doesn't)

### ✅ What Stripe allows you to do

- **Card payments**: Your client can pay by credit card. Easier than a bank transfer.
- **International payments**: Stripe handles international payments. Fees are clear.
- **Automatic invoices**: You can send invoices automatically and Stripe follows up with the client if payment fails.
- **Reports**: Stripe gives you a dashboard with all your payments.
- **Integrations**: You can connect Stripe to Zapier, Make, etc., for automation.

### ❌ What Stripe doesn't allow you to do

- **Free payments**: Stripe takes 2.9% + €0.30 per transaction. It costs money.
- **Small payments**: If you receive €10, Stripe takes €0.59. That's 6% in fees.
- **No bank account**: You must have a French bank account to use Stripe.

**The truth?** For 1 client, Stripe costs more than it saves.

---

## The ROI calculation: Stripe vs Bank Transfer

Let's look at the numbers.

| Element | Cost |
|---|---|
| Bank transfer | €0 |
| Stripe | 2.9% + €0.30 per transaction |
| **Difference** | **2.9% + €0.30** |

Now, the real question: **From what amount does Stripe become worthwhile?**

### Case 1: You have 1 client and they pay you €1000/month

**Bank transfer:** €0 in fees. You receive €1000.

**Stripe:** 2.9% + €0.30 = €29 + €0.30 = €29.30 in fees. You receive €970.70.

**Difference:** €29.30/month = €351.60/year.

**Verdict:** Bank transfer. It's much more profitable.

### Case 2: You have 10 clients and they pay by card

**Bank transfer:** €0 in fees. But you have to manually follow up if a client forgets.

**Stripe:** 2.9% + €0.30 per transaction. But you get automatic invoices and automatic reminders.

**Time saved:** 30 min/month (no manual follow-ups).

**Stripe fees:** If you receive €10,000/month, Stripe takes €290 + €3 = €293/month = €3516/year.

**ROI:** €3516/year for 6h/year = €586/hour saved. This is profitable if you charge >€586/h. (Spoiler: no.)

**Verdict:** Bank transfer + manual follow-ups. It's more profitable.

### Case 3: You have international clients

**Bank transfer:** International transfer fees can be €20-50 per transaction.

**Stripe:** 2.9% + €0.30. No additional fees for international payments.

**Difference:** Stripe can save €20-50 per international payment.

**Verdict:** Stripe for international payments. Bank transfer for French payments.

---

## The ToolTrim recommendation

**No. You don't need Stripe if you have fewer than 5 clients and they can all pay by bank transfer.**

Here's why:

1. **Stripe costs 2.9% + €0.30 per transaction.** For a solo freelancer, that's expensive.

2. **Bank transfer is free.** No fees. The money arrives directly.

3. **French clients know how to make a bank transfer.** No need for Stripe for that.

**When you should switch to Stripe:**

- You have international clients
- You want automatic invoices and automatic reminders
- You want a dashboard with all your payments

**Until then, stick to bank transfer. Seriously.**

---

## What we would do in your place

If you've just signed your first client:

1. **Ask for a bank transfer.** It's free. Give them your IBAN.

2. **Send an invoice with your invoice.** Include your IBAN and the due date.

3. **Follow up after 7 days if payment hasn't arrived.** Politely. "Just to confirm you received my invoice?"

4. **Use a spreadsheet to track your payments.** Google Sheets. Free. Add a "Paid" column for each invoice.

5. **Revisit the question in 6 months.** If you have 5+ international clients, switch to Stripe.

---

## Conclusion

Stripe costs 2.9% + €0.30 per transaction. For 1 client, you won't earn enough to justify these fees. Bank transfer is sufficient for you. Use that money for something else. Really.

But if you have international clients? Then Stripe pays for itself. That's fair.

# Looking for the most cost-effective AI for your tasks: ChatGPT, Claude, or DeepSeek?

## The Scene

It's Wednesday afternoon. You have 3 urgent tasks:

1. Write a business proposal (2000 words)
2. Proofread and improve an article (1500 words)
3. Generate 10 LinkedIn content ideas

You open your browser. You see ChatGPT. You see Claude. You see DeepSeek. You ask yourself: "Which one is the most cost-effective for my tasks?"

That's a good question. And the answer is not "it depends."

---

## The real problem: you're confusing "having a better AI" with "having the most cost-effective AI for your specific tasks"

Most freelancers think one AI is better than another. That Claude is "smarter" than ChatGPT. That DeepSeek is "cheaper."

False.

The problem isn't choosing the "best" AI. The problem is choosing the most cost-effective AI for your specific tasks. Because each AI excels in different areas.

---

## Comparison: ChatGPT vs Claude vs DeepSeek

### ChatGPT (OpenAI)

**Pricing:**
- Free: GPT-3.5 (slow, less intelligent)
- Plus: $20/month = GPT-4 (fast, very intelligent)
- API: $0.03 for 1K input tokens, $0.06 for output

**Strengths:**
- **General writing:** ChatGPT is excellent for writing emails, articles, business proposals.
- **Speed:** ChatGPT is very fast. You get a response in 5-10 seconds.
- **Availability:** ChatGPT is always available. No overload.
- **Integrations:** ChatGPT integrates everywhere (Zapier, Make, etc.).

**Weaknesses:**
- **Cost:** $20/month for Plus. That's expensive for a solo freelancer.
- **Hallucinations:** ChatGPT sometimes invents facts. You need to verify.
- **Limited context:** ChatGPT forgets context after 10-15 messages.

**Best for:** General writing, emails, articles, brainstorming.

### Claude (Anthropic)

**Pricing:**
- Free: Claude 3 Haiku (slow, less intelligent)
- Paid: $20/month = Claude 3 Opus (fast, very intelligent)
- API: $0.03 for 1K input tokens, $0.15 for output

**Strengths:**
- **Long context:** Claude can process 100K tokens. That's huge. You can give it an entire document.
- **Nuanced analysis:** Claude is excellent for analyzing complex texts, data, abstract concepts.
- **Fewer hallucinations:** Claude invents fewer facts than ChatGPT.
- **Safety:** Claude is more cautious. It more often refuses problematic requests.

**Weaknesses:**
- **Cost:** $20/month for Opus. Same price as ChatGPT Plus.
- **Slowness:** Claude is slower than ChatGPT. You wait 10-20 seconds for a response.
- **Fewer integrations:** Claude integrates less well than ChatGPT.

**Best for:** Complex text analysis, article proofreading, nuanced writing.

### DeepSeek (DeepSeek)

**Pricing:**
- Free: DeepSeek V2 (slow, less intelligent)
- Paid: $0.14 for 1M input tokens, $0.28 for output

**Strengths:**
- **Ultra-low cost:** DeepSeek is 100x cheaper than ChatGPT or Claude.
- **Decent performance:** DeepSeek V2 is almost as good as GPT-4 for many tasks.
- **No subscription:** You pay per use. No $20/month.

**Weaknesses:**
- **Slowness:** DeepSeek is very slow. You wait 20-30 seconds for a response.
- **Fewer integrations:** DeepSeek integrates less well than ChatGPT.
- **Less context:** DeepSeek can process fewer tokens than Claude.
- **Less reliable:** DeepSeek is less stable than ChatGPT or Claude.

**Best for:** Simple tasks, brainstorming, maximum savings.

---

## The ROI calculation: ChatGPT vs Claude vs DeepSeek

Let's look at the numbers for 3 common tasks.

### Task 1: Write a business proposal (2000 words)

| AI | Time | Cost | Cost/hour |
|---|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT Plus | 15 min | $0.33 | $1.32/h |
| Claude Opus | 20 min | $0.45 | $1.35/h |
| DeepSeek | 30 min | $0.04 | $0.08/h |

**Verdict:** DeepSeek is 10x cheaper. But you wait 2x longer. If you charge €50/h, you lose €0.50 in time. But you save €0.29 in cost. Net: you lose €0.21. Not cost-effective.

### Task 2: Proofread and improve an article (1500 words)

| AI | Time | Cost | Cost/hour |
|---|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT Plus | 10 min | $0.25 | $1.50/h |
| Claude Opus | 15 min | $0.35 | $1.40/h |
| DeepSeek | 25 min | $0.03 | $0.07/h |

**Verdict:** Claude is better for nuanced analysis. ChatGPT is faster. DeepSeek is cheaper but too slow.

### Task 3: Generate 10 LinkedIn content ideas

| AI | Time | Cost | Cost/hour |
|---|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT Plus | 5 min | $0.15 | $1.80/h |
| Claude Opus | 8 min | $0.20 | $1.50/h |
| DeepSeek | 15 min | $0.02 | $0.08/h |

**Verdict:** ChatGPT is the fastest. DeepSeek is the cheapest but too slow.

---

## ToolTrim's Recommendation

**Here's what we would do in your shoes:**

### If you charge €30-50/h

**Use ChatGPT Plus.**

Why? Because time is money. ChatGPT Plus is 2x faster than DeepSeek. If you save 10 min per task, you save €5 (at €30/h). Stripe fees ($0.33) are negligible.

**Cost:** $20/month = €240/year

**Time saved:** 5-10h/month

**ROI:** €240/year for 60-120h/year = €2-4/hour saved. This is cost-effective if you charge >€30/h.

### If you charge €15-30/h

**Use free ChatGPT + DeepSeek.**

Why? Because you need to save every euro. Free ChatGPT is free. DeepSeek is ultra-cheap. Combine the two.

**Cost:** €0

**Time saved:** 3-5h/month (less than with Plus, but free)

**ROI:** €0/year. It's free.

### If you charge €50+/h

**Use Claude Opus.**

Why? Because Claude is better for nuanced analysis. If you do complex writing, article proofreading, data analysis, Claude is your best friend.

**Cost:** $20/month = €240/year

**Time saved:** 8-12h/month (Claude is better for complex tasks)

**ROI:** €240/year for 96-144h/year = €1.67-2.5/hour saved. This is cost-effective if you charge >€50/h.

---

## What we would do in your shoes

1. **Test ChatGPT Plus for 1 month.** Measure your time saved. Calculate the ROI.

2. **Test DeepSeek for 1 month.** Measure your time saved. Calculate the ROI.

3. **Choose the most cost-effective AI for your specific tasks.** Not the "best" AI. The most cost-effective.

4. **Combine 2 AIs if necessary.** ChatGPT for quick writing. Claude for nuanced analysis. DeepSeek for maximum savings.

5. **Revisit the question every 3 months.** AIs improve. Prices change. Tasks change.

---

## Conclusion

There is no "best" AI. There is the most cost-effective AI for your specific tasks.

- **ChatGPT Plus:** Best for quick writing. $20/month.
- **Claude Opus:** Best for nuanced analysis. $20/month.
- **DeepSeek:** Best for maximum savings. $0.14 for 1M tokens.

Choose the one that saves you the most time. Not the one that is "best."

# You're a freelance writer: here's the minimal stack that's actually enough for you

## The scene

It's Monday morning. You have 3 active clients. You need to write 5 articles this week. You also need to manage your invoices, your deadlines, and your client emails.

You look at your computer. You have 12 applications open. Notion, Google Docs, Grammarly, Canva, Calendly, Stripe, ChatGPT, Gmail, Slack, Loom, 1Password, and Zapier.

You think: "Do I really use all these tools? How much am I paying per month for all this?"

You open a spreadsheet. You add it up. $240 + $120 + $144 + $120 + $96 + $29 + $36 + $15 + $20 + $12.50 + $36 + $15 = **$883/month**.

Almost $900 a month. For what? To write articles.

It's too much. And you know it.

---

## The real problem: you're confusing "having tools" with "having a work system"

Most freelance writers think they need all these tools. That each tool solves a specific problem. That without them, they can't work.

Wrong.

The problem isn't the tools. The problem is that you don't have a system. You add a tool every time you encounter a problem. You never delete anything. You accumulate.

Result? $883/month for a solo writer who makes $3,000/month. That's 29% of your income going to tools.

Here's the truth: a freelance writer only needs **5 tools**. Not 12. Not 8. Five.

---

## The minimal stack for freelance writers

### 1. Google Docs (free)

**Why:** It's your text editor. It's where you write your articles.

**Cost:** $0

**Alternatives:** Notion, Microsoft Word, Hemingway Editor. But Google Docs is free and sufficient.

**What it does:**
- Collaborative editing (your clients can comment)
- Version history (you can go back)
- Export to PDF (to send to your clients)
- Easy sharing (shareable link)

**What it doesn't do:**
- Advanced grammar checking (you'll use Grammarly for that)
- Idea generation (you'll use ChatGPT for that)

**Verdict:** Keep it. It's free and it works.

### 2. ChatGPT Plus ($20/month = $240/year)

**Why:** It's your writing assistant. You use it to generate ideas, write introductions, correct texts.

**Cost:** $20/month

**Alternatives:** Claude Opus ($20/month), DeepSeek (ultra-cheap), Perplexity (free for search).

**What it does:**
- Generate content ideas
- Write introductions and conclusions
- Correct and improve texts
- Translate
- Explain complex concepts

**What it doesn't do:**
- Write the entire article (you need to do that yourself)
- Check grammar (use Grammarly for that)

**Verdict:** Keep it. It's profitable if you use it 1h+/day.

### 3. Grammarly ($12/month = $144/year)

**Why:** It's your grammar checker. You use it to catch mistakes you miss.

**Cost:** $12/month

**Alternatives:** LanguageTool (free), Antidote ($99/year), Reverso (free).

**What it does:**
- Detect spelling and grammar errors
- Suggest a more professional tone
- Check for plagiarism (Premium)

**What it doesn't do:**
- Write for you
- Generate ideas

**Verdict:** Keep it. For a writer, it's essential.

### 4. Notion (free)

**Why:** It's your project management system. You use it to track your articles, deadlines, clients.

**Cost:** $0 (free)

**Alternatives:** Airtable (free), Monday.com (paid), Asana (paid).

**What it does:**
- Create a database of your articles (title, status, deadline, client)
- Create a database of your clients (contact, hourly rate, articles written)
- Create an editorial calendar
- Track your invoices

**What it doesn't do:**
- Write for you
- Check your grammar

**Verdict:** Keep it. It's free and you can manage your entire business inside it.

### 5. Stripe (free, commission per transaction)

**Why:** It's how you get paid. You use it to create invoices and receive payments.

**Cost:** Free, but 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

**Alternatives:** Bank transfer (free), PayPal (3.49% + $0.49), Wise (free for transfers).

**What it does:**
- Create automatic invoices
- Receive card payments
- Track your income
- Manage your clients

**What it doesn't do:**
- Write for you
- Check your grammar

**Verdict:** Keep it. It's profitable if you have international clients.

---

## What you should cancel immediately

### Canva Pro ($120/year)

**Why you have it:** You thought you needed to create images for your articles.

**Why you should cancel it:** 95% of your articles don't need images. And when you do, ChatGPT can generate images now.

**Savings:** $120/year

### Calendly Pro ($96/year)

**Why you have it:** You thought you needed to schedule client meetings.

**Why you should cancel it:** You can use Google Calendar (free). Or simply ask your clients to propose time slots.

**Savings:** $96/year

### Loom ($120/year)

**Why you have it:** You thought you needed to record videos for your clients.

**Why you should cancel it:** You probably never recorded a video. And if you need to, QuickTime (free on Mac) or OBS (free) are enough.

**Savings:** $120/year

### 1Password ($36/year)

**Why you have it:** You thought you needed a password manager.

**Why you should cancel it:** Google Password Manager (free) does the same thing. Or just use your browser's built-in password manager.

**Savings:** $36/year

### Zapier ($15/month = $180/year)

**Why you have it:** You thought you needed to automate your workflows.

**Why you should cancel it:** You probably never created an automation. And if you need to, Make (free) or IFTTT (free) are enough.

**Savings:** $180/year

### Slack ($12.50/month = $150/year)

**Why you have it:** You thought you needed to communicate with your clients.

**Why you should cancel it:** Email is enough. Or WhatsApp (free). Or Telegram (free).

**Savings:** $150/year

---

## The calculation: how much you save

| Tool | Current cost | Minimal cost | Savings |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google Docs | $0 | $0 | $0 |
| ChatGPT Plus | $240/year | $240/year | $0 |
| Grammarly | $144/year | $144/year | $0 |
| Notion | $0 | $0 | $0 |
| Stripe | Commission | Commission | $0 |
| Canva Pro | $120/year | $0 | $120 |
| Calendly Pro | $96/year | $0 | $96 |
| Loom | $120/year | $0 | $120 |
| 1Password | $36/year | $0 | $36 |
| Zapier | $180/year | $0 | $180 |
| Slack | $150/year | $0 | $150 |
| **TOTAL** | **$883/year** | **$624/year** | **$259/year** |

**You save $259 per year. That's $21.60 per month.**

It doesn't seem like much. But it's $259 you can use for:
- A copywriting course ($200)
- A better computer ($1,000 over 4 years)
- A rate increase (you can charge $5 more per article)

---

## The minimal stack in action

Here's how you work with this stack:

### Monday morning: planning

1. Open Notion
2. Add the 5 articles you need to write this week
3. Add the deadlines
4. Add the clients

**Time:** 10 minutes

### Monday-Friday: writing

1. Open Google Docs
2. Use ChatGPT to generate an introduction
3. Write the body of the article
4. Use ChatGPT to generate a conclusion
5. Use Grammarly to check grammar
6. Send to your client

**Time:** 2-3 hours per article

### Friday evening: invoicing

1. Open Stripe
2. Create an invoice for each client
3. Send the invoice by email

**Time:** 15 minutes

### Total per week: 3h30 of work + 25 minutes of admin

---

## The ToolTrim recommendation

**Cancel Canva Pro, Calendly Pro, Loom, 1Password, Zapier, and Slack immediately.**

You'll save $259 per year. That's money you can use for something more useful.

Keep only:
- **Google Docs** (free): your text editor
- **ChatGPT Plus** ($240/year): your writing assistant
- **Grammarly** ($144/year): your grammar checker
- **Notion** (free): your project management system
- **Stripe** (commission): your payment platform

That's all you need. Honestly.

---

## What we would do in your place

1. **Export all your projects from Notion.** Make sure you have a local backup.
